title: Raise a tilt steering wheel two notches: pull the lock lever down, lift the drooping wheel, push the lever up to lock it
instruction: Pull the tilt lever under the steering column down, raise the wheel two notches, then push the lever back up so the column locks there, and take your hands off the wheel and lever.
context: Every driver who shares a car resets the wheel before driving, and fleet, bus and truck drivers do it at the start of each shift: about 2.2 million US heavy and tractor-trailer truck drivers (BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook; many heavy-truck columns tilt by an air foot valve, so an upper bound) and 233 million licensed US drivers (FHWA Highway Statistics 2023). Kia's 2022 Sonet (QY) owner's manual (Tilt steering wheel) gives the steps: pull the lock-release lever down, set the wheel's angle, pull the lever up to lock it, then push the wheel up and down to check that it is locked. Mazda's CX-3 manual gives the same: pull the lever under the column down, tilt the wheel, push the lever up to lock; if the lever is hard to raise, rock the wheel lightly so the teeth mesh.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the bench top. (1) A dashboard block, x 56 to 70, y -35 to 35, 36 high, fixed. (2) A tilt steering column hinged inside it at x 58.9, height 21.8, rising toward the robot at 23 degrees from horizontal, 3 kg with its wheel, a counterbalance spring leaving about 1.2 N m of droop; it tilts 0 to 12 degrees with lock notches every 3 degrees and starts locked at 0. (3) A 370 mm steering wheel (25 mm rim, three spokes: left, right, down) on the column, its centre at x 35, y 0, height 32. (4) The tilt lock lever under the column on the robot's left: a 70 mm arm and a 45 x 45 mm paddle 10.5 cm along the column from its hinge, at y 8.5; it swings down 25 degrees to open, stays where it is left (1.0 N m friction, about 15 N at the paddle, an estimate), and unlocks the column past 10 degrees down. Closing it within 0.3 degrees of a notch locks the column there; opened, the column is free and falls to its lowest notch under its weight (in the sim it never springs up; the real build is a droop-type column, droop checked with the 5 N scale at the rim). (5) A yellow tape mark on the dashboard face at the rim-top height of notch 3. Modelled on the 2022 Kia Sonet (QY) and Mazda CX-3 tilt columns. A real build: a used tilt column with wheel from a salvage yard, typically under USD 150 (estimate), bolted to a bench frame.
scoring: Judged on the state at the end; only failures latch (the void, or a lock that moves under the test push). Raised: column angle over 1.5 degrees (0.33). Locked at the target: the lock engaged at notch 3 (6 degrees, within 0.3), the lever closed (within 3 degrees of its stop), held 1 s (0.67). Done: also a lattice of points 2 to 3 cm apart over each gripper (fingertips, pads, palm, housing) at least 3 cm from the wheel, column and lever, and a 5 N push down the arc at the rim top moves the column less than 1 degree over 0.5 s (1.0). Void: the column locks onto a notch while moving faster than 3 degrees per second with no gripper within 3 cm of the wheel rim or hub (a dropped wheel); a held wheel carried through a notch does not void. Real trial: notch 3 is the second position above the lowest (on finer teeth, its gauge reading measured at setup): angle gauge 6 +/- 0.3 degrees above the start reading, rim top level with the dashboard tape mark in a side photo; hands clear means no part of either gripper within 3 cm of the wheel, column or lever, judged from the end photo or video (the point lattice is sim only); the void is judged from video (the column still moving when it locks onto a notch, with no gripper within about 3 cm of the rim, spokes or hub); a digital angle gauge (0.1 degree, about USD 30) on the column shroud, and a 5 N spring scale at the rim.
run_limit: 1,200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches 1.0 at step 585 (29.25 s) on an RTX 3090 Ti.
reset_notes: About 20 s, nothing consumed: pull the lever down, lower the wheel by the rim to its lowest notch, push the lever up and check the wheel will not move. No hidden variables; no seed changes the scene.
fidelity: Wheel and column at typical car size, shaped from the owner's-manual figures of a 2022 Kia Sonet (QY) and a Mazda CX-3 (no CAD); no published wheel size, column angle or spring. Estimates: column angle, 3 kg moving mass, counterbalance spring, five notches 3 degrees apart, lever travel and friction. The lock is a stiff joint lock engaged when the lever closes within 0.3 degrees of a notch, not modelled teeth; the lever itself is a colliding hinged body that the hand must move.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (1 trial, 1,200 steps, session held); demo: 1.0
